messages:
Ella: Hey team — on the Acero POC. Client reports the embeddings+rerank endpoint keeps returning 400s and occasional 429s when they send batched encoded vectors. They say "dims mismatch" in the app logs. Can engineering swarm? :pray:
Raj: Copy. Can you paste the exact request body they're sending? Also which encoder binary/version are they using?
Ella: Here, truncated: 
```
POST /v1/models/redwood-embed-512/encode
{
  \"input\": ["doc1","doc2"],
  \"return_embeddings\": true,
  \"batch_size\": 64
}
\nPOST /v1/rerank
{
  \"query\": \"how to onboard\",
  \"candidates\": [[...embedding vectors...]]
}
```
They said their encoder returns 768-dim vectors. Model is redwood-embed-512.
Marta: That immediately explains dims mismatch — they're sending 768 vectors to a 512-dim model. Two options: (1) re-run their encoder with the 512 model checkpoint OR (2) run a projection step server-side to map 768->512 but that's approx and not ideal for production.
Kevin: Also the 429s likely due to their client using aggressive batching + no retry/backoff. The request shows batch_size 64 with long vectors; server may hit per-request token/compute limits. We should ask for exact error payloads from the API.
Ella: They attached last error body: 
```
{
  \"error\": \"embedding_dim_mismatch\",
  \"message\": \"expected embedding dim 512 but got 768\"
}
```
Raj: OK. I'll DM them to switch encoder config. In parallel, we can add a temporary guard in our rerank endpoint to return a clearer error code and suggest suggested dims in the message. Marta, any quick server-side mitigation?
Marta: We can add a soft-fail translation path that rejects mismatched dims with a suggested payload example. Short-term we can add a diagnostic header `X-Embed-Dims: expected=512 got=768` in error responses.
Kevin: For rate limits, tell them to reduce batch_size to 8-16 and implement exponential backoff (500ms -> 1s). Also verify they aren't hitting per-minute request limits — I can check their tenant metrics.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: rerank-error-enhancements v2.3.1 to staging — started by @Kevin — ETA ~15m.
Kevin: Pushed a quick fix to make the error message clearer and include the dims header. Also added a metric that counts "dim_mismatch" events.
Ella: Client asks about pricing impact if they have to re-encode documents (they have ~2.5M docs). Any guidance?
Raj: Re-encoding cost estimate: token/embedding compute + storage. Rough calc — at 2.5M docs * average 200 tokens/doc, embedding unit cost X => we'll produce a ballpark in the next 24h. Also propose incremental approach: re-encode new docs and lazy migrate old ones prioritized by usage.
Marta: Also advise using our batch-encoding job runner (dedicated dedicated capacity) for cheaper throughput. We can offer a discounted reserved slot for the POC period; I'll add that to the proposal.
Ella: Client also sent a security Q: can we confirm embeddings aren't persisted outside tenant storage and that server-side projection won't export vectors?
Kevin: Yes — embeddings are stored in the customer's tenant blob. Any temporary in-memory projection/transformation is ephemeral and not persisted unless they opt in. We'll provide a short security note for their questionnaire.
Ella: I'll send the immediate remediation steps to the customer: 1) stop sending 768-dim vectors to the 512 model, 2) downgrade batch_size to 8-16, 3) add retry/backoff.
Raj: I'll draft a concise how-to with example requests and a cost estimate.
Marta: Follow-up: we should add a small doc in our public how-to about common embedding dim pitfalls — this one comes up a lot when customers swap encoders.
Ella: Great. Thanks everyone — I'll loop the customer in and update thread after they try fixes. :thumbsup:
